On October 11, our team visited families whose tents had been burned, leaving them without shelter once again. Even as we filmed, heavy gunfire echoed around us. This is the reality of life in Gaza. Families who have lost everything continue to live under the threat of violence, yet refuse to be driven from their land. This is what steadfastness looks like. Sumud. A determination that is difficult to comprehend unless you understand what it means to face the loss of your homeland. They have burned their shelters, destroyed their neighborhoods, and displaced them again and again. But they have not broken their connection to Palestine. They are not leaving. Israeli forces have arrested journalist and activist Andrey X while he was helping a Palestinian farmer harvest olives in Taybeh, east of Ramallah, in the occupied West Bank yesterday. More than 12 soldiers and police officers entered the grove to stop the farmer from picking olives. A police unit arrived around 30 minutes later and forcibly arrested Andrey. He was later released after being detained on suspicion of publicly identifying with a terrorist organisation. His arrest comes amid a sharp increase in Israeli settler attacks and crop theft targeting Palestinian farmers during the annual olive harvest, alongside military restrictions preventing access to their land.

During a public campus event, conservative commentator Charlie Kirk debated a student regarding the national identity and existence of Palestine. Kirk initiated the exchange by asking the student to define the specific ethnicity of Palestinians. The student identified Palestinians as Arabs whose identity stems from being born in Palestine or having Palestinian parents. Kirk countered this by stating he does not believe the place exists, referring to the region strictly as "Judea and Samaria". This exchange highlights a contentious geopolitical disagreement common in modern political discourse. The core debate centers on competing historical narratives, territorial claims, and the international recognition of statehood, topics that frequently ignite ideological divides across American universities. The interaction concluded when the student asked if Palestine has a right to exist. Kirk affirmed that individuals have a right to exist but reiterated his claim that Palestine is a "non-existent place". This underscores ongoing disputes over historical terminology. #CharlieKirk #TurningPointUSA #Geopolitics #CampusDebate #MiddleEastDiscourse
